parsed.language: English, with French and German proper names
parsed.estimated_period: c. 1920s–1930s (inferred from the London postal districts such as 'E. C. 1' and 'S.W. 1', introduced in 1917, and from the Dominion Express Company of Canada, which ceased to exist under that name in the 1920s)

entries.name: Goth & Co.
entries.note: General Agents of the Canadian Pacific Railway Co. and of the Dominion Express Co. of Canada

historical_observations: The use of the English forms 'Basle' and 'Lucerne' and the English headings suggest the directory was aimed at British or English-speaking visitors, residents or traders in Switzerland.

Several well-known Swiss industrial firms appear: Sulzer Frères (Winterthur), Schindler & Co. (Lucerne), Berna motor works (Olten), Thorens (Ste. Croix), and the shipping and forwarding firm Danzas (Basle).

The Canadian Pacific Railway and the Dominion Express Company share the same London address (62-65 Charing Cross), and Goth & Co. of Basle is named as general agent for both, illustrating transatlantic travel and freight links reaching into Switzerland.
Lausanne is strongly represented, including 'Librairie Anglaise' (an English bookshop), which points to the city's sizeable English-speaking community at the time.
Both '3, Place St. François, Lausanne' addresses (Simex and Galland & Co.) are the same, which suggests shared premises or related businesses.
